payload.title: own_pr_ci.is_own_pr_head still decides that an open PR is ARIA's from its head-branch name (aria/, automation/, aria-impl-<hex>) in scan_own_prs and in the repo PR health own_pr flag, a second authorship rule beside merge_record's, so an ARIA change on a person-named branch gets no open-PR CI scan
evidence: aria-kernel/aria_kernel/own_pr_ci.py:109-113 (scan_own_prs skips every open PR whose head name does not match)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/own_pr_ci.py:339 (the repo PR health row's own_pr flag)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/own_pr_ci.py:183-186 (the scan's own docstring: PR #1906 was ARIA's change on a person-named branch)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/merge_record.py:396-405 (the owner's rule: authorship by lineage, not by branch name)
aria-kernel/tests/invariants/test_merge_index_single_owner.py:121-130 (the pin flags the head-prefix rule only inside a function that lists merged PRs)
payload.rule_violated: F3.3a one-owner rule (merge_record.py:396-405): ARIA authorship is decided by merge_record, not by a head branch's name; the merged-PR half was fixed and the open-PR half was left.
payload.notes: ARIA opens a PR and its change reaches GitHub under a branch name the three patterns do not match (the PR #1906 shape the code itself documents). scan_own_prs never snapshots it, so no own-pr-checks row, no CI feedback and no pressure from its red exist while it is open, although the lifecycle's opened row says ARIA opened it; repo PR health records own_pr false for it. Close condition: Decide ownership of an open PR from the lifecycle opened row (merge_record's opened_row and pr_change_binding) instead of its branch name, remove OWN_PR_HEAD_PREFIXES from own_pr_ci, and extend the single-owner invariant to forbid is_own_pr_head outside merge_record; a test that an ARIA-opened PR on a person-named branch is scanned. Verified at origin/main ae2958653d.
